question.text: What are the eligibility criteria for a bank to become a trading member in the currency derivatives segment?

answer.text: Minimum net worth of Rs. 500 crore, CRAR of at least 10%, net NPA not exceeding 3%, and net profit for the last 3 years, with RBI authorization under Section 10 of FEMA
Any bank registered with RBI can become a trading member without additional criteria
Net worth of Rs. 100 crore and registration with SEBI as a stock broker
Net worth of Rs. 50 crore, CRAR of 8%, and no NPA restrictions

explanation.text: The Logic: For a bank to act as a trading member in the currency derivatives segment, the prudential requirements are: minimum net worth of Rs. 500 crore, CRAR of at least 10%, net NPA not exceeding 3%, and net profit for the last 3 years. The bank must also be authorised by RBI under Section 10 of FEMA as an AD Category-I bank. The Trap: Generic stock-broker thresholds are much lower and do not apply to banks in the currency segment. Dropping the net-profit condition is a common omission because the other three numeric thresholds are easier to remember. Note: All four prudential conditions are cumulative; missing any one of them — including the three-year net-profit track record — disqualifies the bank from operating as a TM in this segment.
